text: Plogue, a Canadian software company, have recently released a (software) emulation of the DX-7 in excruciating detail. Here you can see part of the trouble they went through: [VIDEO] . Suffice to say that they used a logic analyzer to discover gritty details that no other analysis of the DX-7 I know has ever paid attention of.

story: Yamaha DX7 chip reverse-engineering, part V: the output circuitry
text: Maybe the closest free plugin, but it's not on the level of accuracy as Plogue's Chipsynth OPS7, which is bit-accurate. The author has an interesting video here, with more to come hopefully: [VIDEO]

story: Reverse-engineering the Yamaha DX7 synthesizer's sound chip from die photos (2021)
text: I would recommend Plogue's OPS7, they have put considerable amounts of time and effort into reverse engineering the original chips. The interface is a little clunky but it sounds fantastic. [LINK] Edit: a YouTube video about the reverse engineering process from David at Plogue: [VIDEO]
